candidate_removed_or_weakened: Entire nitrogen/ammonia disposal (urea cycle support) mechanism removed: Car5a (bicarbonate to CPS1) and Agmat (agmatine/arginine polyamine-urea handling) absent from all candidate mechanisms
Cdo1 reassigned from sulfur amino acid catabolism/nitrogen disposal to bile acid taurine conjugation

decision_relevant_differences: Baseline affirms P25 supports hepatic ammonia/nitrogen disposal via the urea cycle (Car5a->CPS1 bicarbonate, Agmat); candidate provides no basis for this, giving a reader the opposite answer to whether the program handles nitrogen/ammonia detoxification
Cdo1's pathway attribution shifts from general sulfur/nitrogen catabolism to bile acid taurine conjugation, changing which functional axis a reader assigns the gene to
Loss of urea-cycle/nitrogen context regulators (G6pc, Insr) removes the evidence anchoring the dropped nitrogen-disposal theme
assessments.rationale: Both annotations share the dominant frame of a pericentral hepatocyte program coupling Phase I/II detoxification, bile acid/steroid processing, and lipid-droplet/peroxisomal fatty-acid metabolism in an aging/MASLD context, and the candidate genuinely refines the retained themes with gene-specific detail (EET epoxygenase, PPARalpha-regulated Sult2a8, Htatip2, Sord polyol pathway) and TF context. However, the candidate does not merely trim citations or qualify an existing conclusion: it eliminates one of the three named central mechanisms in the baseline — sulfur amino acid catabolism feeding hepatic nitrogen/ammonia disposal and urea-cycle support, built on Cdo1+Car5a+Agmat. Car5a and Agmat disappear entirely, and Cdo1 is re-attributed to a bile acid taurine-conjugation axis. This is an affirmative, biologically distinct functional claim (ammonia/urea handling) that a reader of the candidate would no longer draw, and Cdo1's pathway reassignment changes attribution of a shared gene. Because a reader could reach a different biological decision about whether P25 participates in nitrogen/ammonia detoxification, this exceeds refinement and constitutes a material change to a central program mechanism. This resolves the prior disagreement in favor of the materially_changed call: the secondary assessor correctly identified the same removals but under-weighted that the removed item was a distinctly named central mechanism carrying an independent functional conclusion, not a peripheral qualifier.
shared_core_conclusions: Coordinated Phase I/II xenobiotic detoxification battery (Cyp2c50, Aldh1a1, Aldh3a2, Gsta3, Akr1c6) characteristic of pericentral hepatocytes
Bile acid/steroid sulfation via SULT2A enzymes supports biliary/urinary elimination
Lipid droplet biogenesis (Fitm1) coupled to peroxisomal/ER fatty acid oxidation (Eci2, Hao2, Cyb5b)
Cdo1 channels cysteine catabolism toward taurine production
Program interpreted in a pericentral hepatocyte aging/MASLD context
